findings.problem: UI, route and alias import private core storage.
findings.principle: AGENTS.md:1 and DESIGN.md:3 require public core and no UI storage. Automated import resolution plus review; no private import exception.

findings.fix: Expose a useful checkout capability through existing packages/core/index.ts; migrate web consumers, keeping storage private. Do not merely re-export storage representation or add forwarding layers.

findings.problem: Route owns pricing, bulk discount, mutable order persistence and response mapping.
findings.principle: Proposed responsibility rule: core owns pricing/order creation; web maps transport. Human review and public checkout compatibility. Exceptions require named scope/reason/removal condition.
findings.consequence: Pricing and persistence changes both edit the route; shared mutable array is an implicit owner.
findings.fix: Move pricing and order recording behind one core checkout interface; keep HTTP-shaped response mapping in the route. Candidate checkout.ts and private orders.ts only if selected. Preserve current public shape and investigate broader pricing before altering it.
findings.verification: Capture approved checkout before/after, then check public outcome and boundary rule. Persistence semantics and bulk outcomes need authoritative acceptance before extra tests.

findings.problem: Core a and b mutually recurse with no terminating branch, independently of checkout.
findings.principle: Proposed core dependency rule: forbid unintended cycles; native boundary check and responsibility review. Exceptions require a documented legitimate dependency and removal condition.
findings.consequence: Calling either function cannot produce a finite result; coupled core files block a clean graph check. No evidence that they affect checkout execution.
findings.fix: Determine intended capability before consolidating into one cohesive owner, redirecting dependencies, or selecting removal of unused code. No invented return value.
findings.verification: Native cycle check must become clean; if retained, test its approved public capability. Current functions have no acceptance source, so semantic repair stays blocked.

findings.problem: Core database module mixes static price policy and external HTTP price fetching; entry exports storage function directly.
findings.principle: Proposed information-hiding rule: core pricing owns business decisions and a private adapter owns fetch. Review public interface and acceptance; exceptions need narrow reason and expiry.
findings.consequence: Service shape and price-policy knowledge are bound to a storage-named module and exposed to callers.
findings.fix: Keep current package entry; place policy in a cohesive core owner and isolate external fetch only where it hides actual complexity. No new framework, deployment or service. Public quote()=12 is observed, not approved checkout policy.
findings.verification: Protect existing approved checkout through real loopback HTTP and public core entry; approve quote/service failure semantics before new expectations. A live external endpoint is unavailable.

findings.verification: Owner confirmation of meanings followed by exact glossary diff review; no code rename bundled.
